name: MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 Procedure I low-temperature storage of explosives/munitions at the Severe Cold (C3) extreme, -51 C, for at least 72 h after stabilization
plain_name: Store explosives and munitions at -51 C for three days to check they stay safe
description: Procedure I (Storage) of MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 applied to explosives, munitions, rubber and plastics, which the method says may keep deteriorating after temperature stabilization and therefore need a minimum storage period of 72 hours. The storage temperature is the Severe Cold (C3) design value of -51 C from Table 502.7-I (also the 20 % frequency-of-occurrence extreme of Table 502.7-II), reached at no more than 3 C/min, followed by return to ambient, visual examination and operational checkout.
keywords: Store explosives and munitions at -51 C for three days to check they stay safe

sources.citation: MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 Low Temperature (Department of Defense Test Method Standard, 31 January 2019)

requirements.rationale: The item is stored at the C3 storage/transit temperature of -51 C (222.15 K).
The machine's lowest temperature must be -51 C (222.15 K) or colder.
Explosives/munitions need at least 72 h at -51 C after stabilization, so the chamber must run unattended that long; continuous-run capability is rarely documented, so not mandatory.
